articles.title: KPop Demon Hunters Is Getting Yet Another Immersive Gaming Experience in Early 2027
articles.summary: Immersive Gamebox is teaming up with Netflix to bring fans into the world of KPop Demon Hunters. A new interactive gaming experience based on the animated streaming hit will launch across select U.S. locations in January 2027.
articles.body:
Immersive Gamebox is teaming up with Netflix to bring fans into the world of KPop Demon Hunters. A new interactive gaming experience based on the animated streaming hit will launch across select U.S. locations in January 2027.

According to a press release, the experience will have players “move, react, and work together through a series of interactive games featuring 3D motion tracking, projection mapping, touch-sensitive walls and spatial audio.” The experience avoids heavy VR goggles, instead using lightweight motion-tracking headsets.

Before getting into actual gameplay, players will get to create their own ‘Superfan’ avatar in the style of the animated movie. Then, HUNTR/X will guide participants on a quest to protect the Honmoon. The experience will feature familiar locations, moments, and characters from the movie while requiring participants to work together on minigames and activities.

The full KPop Demon Hunters experience is designed for two to six players with an estimated run time of 60 minutes. Tickets will be available in December, but fans can already sign up to join a Priority Waitlist that will offer 24 hours of early access before the general sale.

Immersive Gamebox launched in London before opening its first U.S. location in 2020. The company really hit its stride with licensed collaborations, having previously worked with Netflix on its Squid Game and Floor Is Lava experiences. It now hosts over 29 experiences at 35 venues.

“KPop Demon Hunters perfectly captures what we do best: transforming the world’s most exciting stories into shared experiences that friends and families can play together," said Lisa Paton, CEO of Immersive Gamebox. "Music, movement, and the collective energy of the fans are such a huge part of this film, and we can’t wait for fans to join the action and become part of the story.”

This isn’t fans’ only opportunity to help Huntr/x protect the Honmoon. Netflix will be hosting its own KPop Demon Hunters: The Immersive Experience at two Netflix House locations this November. The Netflix experience will make use of "3D technology" while also featuring live actors, multiple sets, and themed food and drinks.

Both immersive experiences will stick to the movie's original Honmoon story, though we'll be getting more action in the world of KPop Demon Hunters soon enough. Well, maybe not too soon. Reports suggest the sequel may not release until at least 2029 . At the very least, Netflix has already agreed to correct its previous mistakes by giving KPop Demon Hunters 2 a full theatrical release .

articles.title: Mass Effect 5 Details Revealed Following Cancellation, Including 'Hitman-Style Freedom' in Missions
articles.summary: Following the cancellation of Mass Effect 5, purportedly called Mass Effect Universe, last week – alongside the closure of the entire BioWare development studio – new gameplay details about the role-playing game revival have emerged, including handcrafted missions that gave players Hitman-style freedom,  the abililty to hack the environment, brutal close-range executions, the return of Liara, and much more.
articles.body:
Following this week's cancellation of Mass Effect 5, purportedly called Mass Effect Universe – alongside the closure of the entire BioWare development studio – new gameplay details about the role-playing game revival have emerged, including handcrafted missions that gave players Hitman-style freedom, the abililty to hack the environment, brutal close-range executions, the return of Liara, and much more.

YouTube content creator Dantics revealed the details in a new video , as he was a member of the Mass Effect Council – a group of external Mass Effect community members who gave BioWare feedback on the game during development. IGN has verified the legitimacy of these details, and can add that a development source told us that BioWare had "every major [alien] race" working in the build.

Dantics says it "looked incredible" and added , "From what I saw, BioWare was making Mass Effect for us, the fans." More specifically, he shared that the new Mass Effect was set over 600 years after the Reaper War, and your customizable agent was like a John Wick/James Bond-type character who has had experimental technology implanted in you. As a result, you'd be able to hack and manipulate the environment such as letting you "see through walls, identify systems, remotely trigger hazards, and more." Furthermore, you'd also be able to perform "brutal, close-range executions."

Meanwhile, the galaxy has been divided into three major factions, with humanity, the Krogans, the Batarians, and others allied together. The Council races formed their own alliance, while the Geth had emerged as a third superpower who constructed megastructures. Dantics describes the setting of Mass Effect Universe as "a galactic Cold War instead of another Reaper-style invasion with a shadowy adversary."

Missions would've been handcrafted, like in the original trilogy, "but with Hitman-style freedom in how you complete them." Your squadmates would be able to clash with each other, while romance options would return without being "sanitized." Finally, Liara would return from the original trilogy, now as a powerful Asari Matriarch.

BioWare's closure and Mass Effect 5's cancellation have saddened many in the gaming community. I wrote a eulogy about how BioWare was the greatest RPG developer ever . Our own Jackie Thomas lamented that we'll never get to see the series redeemed after the disappointment of Mass Effect Andromeda, and IGN's Matt Purslow believed that EA never knew what it had with BioWare . An internal trailer leaked online following the cancellation that gives us all an idea of what BioWare was building.

Fans aren't giving up yet, though, as an online petition has already surged past 50,000 signatures. In addition, a Canadian politician is calling on the government to support BioWare developers in a buyout that would enable to run the studio independently. We spoke to a number of analysts this week to find out why EA shut BioWare down, and the chances of a franchise selloff .

Ryan McCaffrey is IGN's executive editor of previews and host of IGN's weekly Xbox show, Podcast Unlocked , and a co-host of Next-Gen Console Watch . He's a North Jersey guy, so it's "Taylor ham," not "pork roll." Debate it with him on Twitter at @DMC_Ryan .

articles.title: Magic: The Gathering The Hobbit Gift Bundle Deal Hits Amazon, but You Should Wait for Black Friday
articles.summary: The Magic: The Gathering The Hobbit Gift Bundle is on sale at Amazon, but here is why crunching the numbers proves you should wait for Black Friday before buying.
articles.body:
Magic: The Gathering’s crossovers tend to draw a mixed response from the hardcore fans who want more of Jace, Liliana, and Gideon over the Avengers, but if there’s one crossover that’s been universally praised, it was Lord of the Rings.

Wizards of the Coast looked to follow suit this year with a return to Middle-Earth, and while The Hobbit offers a smaller set than the 2023 original, it’s still packed with great cards. And while this new Amazon deal might be tempting, here’s why we think you’re better off holding your nerve for a few weeks.

This Hobbit x Magic Deal Is Likely To Get Better

Amazon’s latest offering has the Magic x The Hobbit Gift Bundle down from $109.86 to $99.99, a 9% discount .

It’s not the steepest cut we’ve seen, but it does look like a new low price. Inside, you’ll find nine Play Boosters worth $6.99 each, as well as 34 land cards that include full-art seasonal hobbit lands in surge foil and full-art Middle-Earth Journey lands. There’s also an alternate-art promo card, but the real draw is likely to be the Collector Booster.

These can often be priced even higher than the $38 or so you’ll find them for in your local game store, and are the place you’re most likely to unwrap one of the rarest cards in the set , like Gleaming Splendor, The Arkenstone, or Smaug.

Smaug, Wicked Worm (Borderless) (Surge Foil)

Bard, King of Dale (Borderless) (Surge Foil)

Thorin, Mountain-king (Borderless) (Surge Foil)

Thranduil, the Elvenking (Borderless) (Surge Foil)

The Queen of Dale (Showcase) (Surge Foil)

Gandalf, Goblins' Bane (Borderless) (Surge Foil)

The Arkenstone (Borderless) (Surge Foil)

Smaug the Magnificent (Showcase) (Surge Foil)

Gleaming Splendor (Borderless) (Surge Foil)

When you crunch the numbers, you’re not actually saving any more than a couple of bucks on this bundle than buying its separate parts (I’m not factoring in the lands and storage box, admittedly).

With that in mind, this one feels ripe for a discount closer to the sales season. In recent years, we’ve seen Magic sets drop in price, even those launching in the same year. Expect the same to happen here.

articles.title: Xbox Reportedly Asked Netflix for $800 Million for 7-Year Movie and TV Exclusivity Deal
articles.summary: Xbox reportedly asked Netflix for $800 million for a seven-year deal that would have given the streamer exclusive adaptations based on its games.
articles.body:
Xbox reportedly asked Netflix for $800 million for a seven-year deal that would have given the streamer exclusive adaptations based on its games.

Details on the behind-the-scenes dealings between the two entertainment giants came from a Puck report. The site stated that Netflix, interested in pursuing movie and TV adaptations for some of Microsoft's biggest games, began its offer at $500 million.

What exactly the deal would have yielded outside of the promise to exclusively-licensed Xbox titles for adaptations is unclear, but for Microsoft, it was worth a lot more than what Netflix was willing to offer. Xbox CEO Asha Sharma and her team countered the offer at a staggering $800 million. Following a round of shakeups at Netflix from last week, the deal is said to be completely off the table.

Upcoming New Video Game Movies and TV Shows: 2026 Release Dates and Beyond

It's unclear what exactly led to the deal breaking down, though Puck suggested the exit of Bela Bajaria, who served as content chief until being fired recently, played a role. Now, the site said that Xbox is "pursuing smaller deals with more partners." Who those partners are is a mystery for now.

While Xbox and Netflix were unable to secure a long-term exclusivity deal, both entertainment entities do have plans to work together in the future. A live-action movie and animated series based on Gears of War, for example, have been in the works for some time . In 2024, Netflix announced it was building a Minecraft animated series , and just last month, plans for an animated Diablo series were confirmed .

Xbox shared a statement with Puck: "We have received record-breaking interest in our IP; Netflix is a valued partner and we are excited for the forthcoming release of our Minecraft and Diablo animated series together, among other adaptations."

Netflix announced layoffs impacting around 1,000 staff earlier this month. A few high-profile executives, including Bajaria, were fired just days later. The list also included head of film Dan Lin , who reportedly recently clashed with Barbie director Greta Gerwig about the release of her upcoming Netflix film, Narnia: The Magician's Nephew .

Whether Xbox can manage to find partners for more movie and TV adaptations remains to be seen. In the meantime, you can check out what IGN thought of a few other recent video game adaptations. Capcom's Street Fighter movie , for example, received a 6/10 review , while its Resident Evil movie managed to earn an 8/10 .

articles.title: FemShep Voice Actor Jennifer Hale Speaks Out After Mass Effect 5 Trailer Leaks Online
articles.summary: Award-winning voice actor Jennifer Hale, best known for voicing the female version of Commander Shepard in the first three Mass Effect games, is speaking out after a leaked trailer for the sci-fi franchise’s next title was leaked online.
articles.body:
Award-winning voice actor Jennifer Hale, best known for voicing the female version of Commander Shepard in the first three Mass Effect games, is speaking out after a leaked trailer for the sci-fi franchise’s next title was leaked online.

The Mass Effect community was hit hard this week by news that EA is closing down BioWare , the 30-year-old studio known for spearheading Western RPGs with series like Dragon Age, Mass Effect, Jade Empire, and others.

Rubbing salt in the wound, EA also revealed the next Mass Effect game (supposedly titled Mass Effect Universe) was canceled. This revelation hurt even more after staff who formerly worked on the project spoke out about it online , with one even leaking a full-length trailer for the game on Reddit. This trailer promised a game that would have been everything fans wanted and more — and it even caught the attention of FemShep herself.

Dark Horse Direct's Mass Effect: Tali'Zorah 1/6 Scale Statue - Image Gallery

Hale responded to a re-upload of the Mass Effect 5 trailer on X/Twitter, and it seems she’s just as hopeful as the rest of us that somehow, some way, the game will still get made.

“It's extraordinary,” she wrote . “I’m holding hope for magic to happen. This community and you incredible devs deserve that and more.”

Two days prior, she went live on Instagram alongside fellow Commander Shepard voice actor Mark Meer, who plays the male version of the character, to address fans in the wake of EA’s devastating decision

“I feel weirdly hopeful, and I can’t explain why,” Hale said. “...I feel for the [BioWare] employees who are suddenly unemployed. That is the number one thing on my mind. Those beautiful team members who are looking for a new home.”

“It is very sad news,” Meer added. “It is a massive loss for Edmonton, for Canada, and for the video game industry in general. It’s very unfortunate to see. And of course, I feel very bad for all of the fans.”

“It’s really hard to think about BioWare being shut down, but it was in the hands of ownership that may not have understood what BioWare fully is,” Hale continued. “And I’m hopeful that maybe, there might be some crazy thing where they decide that. in order to increase their profit margins — which is often their priority — they will release these IPs into the market to sell them, and use that to do what they do, which is increase their profit margins. But maybe, someone could grab hold of these IPs and do something with them.”

Hale isn’t alone in this line of thinking; many fans are calling on EA to at least sell BioWare’s intellectual properties to other developers in the hopes that Mass Effect 5 can eventually be released. Even Canadian politicians are getting in on the conversation, with the country’s New Democratic Party leader Avi Lewis taking to social media to publicly call out EA.

However, industry insiders and analysts are urging caution around this particular idea. Speaking with IGN, three separate analysts stated that BioWare’s library of titles simply don’t align with EA’s current strategy, and said it’s unlikely the company relinquishes them to other companies. What’s more, these IPs are likely to be extremely expensive, to the point where other studios simply wouldn’t have the funds nor the time to pursue them.

Former BioWare executive producer Mark Darrah shared a similar sentiment , though he admitted that, given EA is now looking to cut costs to cover its massive debt, it might consider the idea of selling these IPs off — but said it’s just as likely that execs “just try to forget that they ever existed and bury them in the vault.”

Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze .

articles.title: Ahead of GTA 6, PlayStation 5 Sales Were Up 22%, Likely Due To Wolverine
articles.summary: The latter part of 2026 has been packed with excellent games, all leading up to GTA 6 on November 19, so it's not surprising that PS5 sales have jumped over last month.
articles.body:
The latter part of 2026 has been packed with excellent games, all leading up to GTA 6 on November 19, so it's not surprising that PS5 sales have jumped over last month.

PlayStation 5 sales have jumped by 22%, according to a report from Bloomberg, with data from Circana. And, while it's likely that the buildup to GTA 6 has contributed to those sales, it looks like it was September's all-star lineup of games, and particularly Marvel's Wolverine, that were primarily behind the PS5's recent success.

We reached out to Circana Senior Director and Video Game Industry Advisor Mat Piscatella for comment on these recent sales increases, and he told us that despite its middling reception, Wolverine drove quite a bit of hardware sales. "PS5's hardware boost was primarily driven by Marvel's Wolverine. NBA 2K27 and Grand Theft Auto VI also likely helped," he said. However, he added that "Xbox Series did not get a similar sales boost during the month."

When IGN reviewed Wolverine, we gave it a middling 6 out of 10, with reviewer Simon Cardy saying, "Marvel's Wolverine's slick and satisfying combat wears thin well before its conclusion, so much so that even its strong character work can't quite save it from being anything more than okay."

In the weeks that have followed the game's release, the community has also been mixed on the game, and Insomniac has had to respond by fixing some of the more hand-holdy mechanics, like adding a toggle for the ever-present scent trail that guides you to objectives . But, even early on, there were signs that Wolverine was selling .

Now, more than a month after release, Wolverine seems like it was absolutely a success, with Piscatella saying, "For Marvel's Wolverine, [it's] tough to give things a vibe check without understanding folks' frame of reference, but it was the month's best-seller, ranks 11th year-to-date, with a hardware bundle that seems to have sold out and the market's best-selling accessory during the month with the limited edition Marvel's Wolverine DualSense. Seems pretty good to me. But, we'll have to see how the legs are over time. It wasn't as big as say Marvel's Spider-Man 2, but I don't think that would have ever been a reasonable assumption."

That hardware bundle was likely a big reason why PlayStation's sales were so rosy over the last month. The controller looked amazing, and started selling out before the game even launched.

Looking ahead to GTA 6, though, if a game like Wolverine was able to drive hardware like this, I can only imagine that GTA is going to make an even bigger impact. We've already started to see signs of that happening, too. Just a couple of weeks ago, the PS5 Pro started selling out enough that used models started going for as much as $1,400, $500 more than their shelf price. And, to this day, that price still holds, with the PS5 Pro available on both Amazon and Gamestop for $1,399.

At that price, it's going to be interesting to see sales data for this coming month, and how many people are willing to fork over that kind of cash for a new console. After all, there have been rumors this week that the next-generation Xbox Project Helix may cost up to $1,800 . There were also leaks that suggest that for the PS6, just the RAM and SSD alone will cost around $680 , which could see Sony's next-gen console commanding a similar price.

Jackie Thomas is the Senior Tech Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. She's been covering gaming hardware for more than a decade for IGN, TechRadar, Gizmodo, PC Gamer and more. You can follow her @Jackiecobra

articles.title: Miami Vice '85 Has Already Triggered My Fandom in Good and Bad Ways
articles.summary: The latest photos and videos from the set of Miami Vice ‘85 making the rounds on social media reveal Michael B. Jordan and John Leguizamo in costume filming scenes that appear to be faithfully recreating the opening moments of the original TV series pilot.
articles.body:
The latest photos and videos from the set of Miami Vice ‘85 making the rounds on social media reveal Michael B. Jordan and John Leguizamo in costume filming scenes that appear to be faithfully recreating the opening sequence of the original TV series pilot.

Jordan plays New York City police detective Ricardo Tubbs and Leguizamo recently confirmed on his Instagram account that he portrays Esteban Calderone, the Columbian cartel boss who was the antagonist of the series pilot and returned in a later episode of the first season of the 1984-89 TV series . (Fittingly enough, Leguizamo got his big break playing Calderone’s son in the original series .)

The recent batches of set photos and videos from the New York set of Miami Vice ‘85 reveal Jordan and Austin Butler, who plays Tubbs’ future partner Sonny Crockett , shooting the earliest sequences that introduced their respective characters in the original pilot.

It’s been known that Miami Vice ‘85 is inspired by the series’ two-part pilot (“ Brother’s Keeper ”) and the show’s first season in general. The images and footage from the set reveal the movie looks very faithful in those recreations.

John Leguizamo on the set of 'Miami Vice ‘85' 🚨🎬👀 — Miami Vice ‘85 Crave (@MiamiViceCrave) October 23, 2026

John Leguizamo on the set of 'Miami Vice ‘85' 🚨🎬👀

For example, Jordan’s Tubbs is basically wearing the same outfit as original Tubbs actor Philip Michael Thomas wore in the opening scenes of the pilot . Similarly, Leguizamo’s slicked back hair, mustache and cigar are a spot-on nod to Miguel Piñero’s look in the same episode. Beyond the clothes, though, Jordan is recreating the same actions and facial expressions as Thomas’ in the sequence where he runs out into an alley in pursuit of the slippery, enigmatic Calderone . The only major difference is that Jordan’s Tubbs has a beard while the character didn’t grow one until the later seasons of the show.

In the series, Calderone was responsible for the deaths of people close to Crockett and Tubbs so that’s why a New York cop ends up partnering with a Miami Dade P.D. undercover detective. As a lifelong fan of the show, I couldn’t be more excited to see a new Miami Vice movie set in the 1980s and that treats the subject seriously and faithfully. However, a beat-for-beat remake of the TV series pilot could end up being a bit frustrating for fans like myself who know what’s going to happen next and to whom.

Look, my Miami Vice fandom has already gotten the better of me. When the first look images of Jordan and Butler in costume were released, I hastily wrote an op-ed expressing my concern about the dark color palette rather than the pastels that were used in the show’s early seasons. However, my entire thesis was rendered moot just a few hours later when set photos online revealed Butler dressed exactly like Don Johnson’s Sonny Crockett in 1984-85, white suit and all. I had to update my piece with a mea culpa. So I’m concerned I’m similarly rushing to judgment here. Everything from Miami Vice ‘85 looks cool so far and accurate to how it was depicted on the show, but I guess I was hoping for a story that was in the spirit of the show while telling a brand new tale. I’ll just have to wait and see.

Michael Mann’s Miami Vice film from 2006 also riffed on one of the first season’s episodes (“Smuggler’s Blues”) but everything else surrounding that subplot was an entirely new and different experience for fans of the show albeit without the flash and charm that was a hallmark of the series. So I do appreciate that Miami Vice ‘85 is at least going back to its roots.

Miami Vice ‘85 is currently shooting in New York before moving production to Miami, Florida after hurricane season is over. The film opens in theaters on May 19, 2028 .

Jim Vejvoda (he/him) is IGN's Assoc. Director of Entertainment Content.

articles.title: Mass Effect Fans Call for EA Boycott as Petition to Save BioWare's Canceled Game Garners More than 75,000 Signatures
articles.summary: Mass Effect fans are calling for a boycott of all EA products and services in protest of the company closing down BioWare and canceling the next Mass Effect game.
articles.body:
Mass Effect fans are calling for a boycott of all EA products and services in protest of the company closing down BioWare and canceling the next Mass Effect game.

It’s a rough time for Mass Effect fans. On October 21, EA announced its plans to shut down BioWare , a 30-year-old studio that spearheaded RPGs in the West with titles like Dragon Age, Jade Empire, Baldur’s Gate, and of course, Mass Effect .

Players were eagerly awaiting news of the next game in BioWare’s beloved sci-fi franchise — but EA shut that down, too, revealing in a statement that the project was officially canceled.

Dark Horse Direct's Mass Effect: Tali'Zorah 1/6 Scale Statue - Image Gallery

In the two days since then, fans of BioWare and the Mass Effect series have gathered together to call for action, begging EA to at least sell off BioWare’s IP to other studios rather than letting them languish. In fact, tensions have become so strained that players are now calling for an outright boycott of EA’s products and services until something is done.

On Reddit, several threads are rallying Mass Effect fans to gather under the hashtag #savemasseffect, urging players to take action and make their voices heard.

“WE HAVE TO DO SOMETHING! Guys we have to start something here and cry out loud enough that this game can be saved. Either EA making it or selling it off. We have to do it now before the noise on this game quiets down and it becomes another cancelled series, never to return,” one Redditor wrote . “I suggest we start a movement, and message the hell out of EA asking for some kind of outcome that gets this game finished. THIS GAME FINISHED.”

“Mass Effect is one of the better RPGs out today,” another fan wrote in a post titled ‘EA Boycott!’ “...Unless they sell Mass Effect to another studio or bring it back. I will never buy another EA product ever. They are already not one of my favorite studios. No more Respawn Entertainment, DICE, Motive Studios, Criterion Games, Maxis, Full Circle, Cliffhanger Games, or any EA Sports.

“I hope I'm not alone in this. We need to stand up and make our voices heard. I posted on everything I can. We can't let Mass Effect die so easily. Private investors need to realize how badly EA screwed up.”

These calls for a boycott coincide with a fanmade petition urging EA to either sell off the IPs to other developers or hand development of Mass Effect 5 to a different studio. At the time of writing, this petition has garnered over 76,500 signatures and counting as more fans and friends of the industry pile in.

Mass Effect 5 — which was reportedly expected to be called Mass Effect Universe — seems to have already been a good way into its development cycle, judging by a full-length trailer that was leaked online yesterday. This trailer rubbed even more salt in the wound for players, many of whom believed this game would be everything fans had been asking for and more.

Industry vets and even voice actors from the Mass Effect games are speaking out in hopes of somehow, some way, getting this game on shelves. But according to industry analysts and former BioWare bosses , it’s not likely that EA will listen to fans’ demands.

articles.title: Tyrone SFC: Morgan's moment of magic as Edendork make Tyrone history
articles.summary: History made, dreams fulfilled, and a moment that will live forever. With the very last kick, Niall Morgan's sensational two-pointer breaks Errigal Ciaran hearts and crowns Edendork Tyrone Senior Football champions for the first time.
articles.body:
History made, dreams fulfilled, and a moment that will live forever. With the very last kick, Niall Morgan's sensational two-pointer broke Errigal Ciaran hearts and crowned Edendork Tyrone Senior Football Champions for the first time ever.

This was a gripping encounter from the first minute until the last, an unanswered 1-4 before the break, including an expertly dispatched Darren McCurry penalty that brought Edendork from four down, to two ahead at the break summoned a real belief.

A club, a community and a dream started to look like a real possibility. Morgan has won it all with his county Tyrone, including an All-Ireland in 2021 alongside two All-Stars, but doing it for his parish adds extra satisfaction.

"This is the pinnacle. No matter where I go in life, it's Edendork first. Edendork, Tyrone, Ulster, Ireland. It doesn't matter. It's Edendork. People used to say, where are you from? They used to say, a wee place outside Dungannon," Morgan told BBC Sport NI.

"Now it seems like a pretty big place. We just need to get a load of houses built and get all these people into living there and we'd become a super club."

"Impossible to sum up how I feel. As a club we've waited 94 years for this. My 20th season as a senior player.

"Looking at my two kids playing chase on the stairs. What this means to me and this club will never be put in words. I didn't know there was this many people from Edendork. It's going to be a party tonight.

Three late scores including two from Peter Harte edged Errigal one ahead, and it looked like they were going to claim a third title in five seasons right at the last.

But, Edendork were not going to denied their place in history, becoming the second Tyrone club in succession to win their first ever O'Neill Cup title by appearing in their maiden decider.

"Getting to the final after 94 years is just special in itself. To get over the line and finish the job is amazing," Morgan continued.

"Daddy's words to me were, you don't understand, and I don't. You think you do, but for men like that, that turned the pitch 90 degrees to change its direction, took out electric poles, bought land. All you have to do is look around. This is it."

'It feels like you're not going to miss. You feel invincible.'

Edendork's story on their way to winning the O'Neill Cup centred around late, dramatic and vital two-point scores.

In last week's drawn game it finished 0-15 to 1-12 with McCurry's late orange flag from south of 50 metres forcing the replay having eventually been awarded by the referee after a dramatic period of consultation among the officials over a potential breach.

McCurry's contribution today was colossal with 1-6 all coming in the first half, but his faith inspired Morgan's late magic that will be forever etched in the very fabric of Edendork forever more.

"How awesome he was today. I kicked that two-pointer at the end, but he carried us for the majority of the game, so only for him," Morgan said.

"More nerves kicking that one, for sure. (Morgan said of his late winning kick) I was saying, I had pictured Rory Beggan celebrating that one he scored in the Athletic Grounds last year.

"I was thinking, I've got this opportunity to do this for my club now. Darren (McCurry) handed me the ball and he said put that over the bar.

"Whenever Darren does that, it just feels special. It feels like you're not going to miss. You feel invincible. I've told him that before. The confidence he gives me and the rest of his boys."

The season does not end here for Edendork. They will now go to represent the county in the Ulster Club Championship, starting with a preliminary clash against the Down winners Clonduff at Pairc Esler on Saturday 31 October.

articles.title: Xbox’s first chief operating officer is out after just a few months
articles.summary: Helen Chiang is leaving Microsoft after 21 years.
articles.body: Xbox’s first chief operating officer (COO) is leaving after the new role was created just a few months ago. Helen Chiang is leaving Microsoft today, according to an internal Xbox memo seen by The Verge. Chiang has been at Microsoft for 21 years, serving as the head of Minecraft before being promoted to Xbox chief operating officer in July. Xbox CEO Asha Sharma announced Chiang’s departure in a surprisingly short memo today. “Helen Chiang is leaving Microsoft today. I’m grateful for her years of service and wish her well,” said Sharma. As Chiang is departing today, her immediate responsibilities are being split up between other Xbox leaders for now, and Sharma notes that “We’ll share more on COO leadership as plans are finalized.” That sounds like the COO position isn’t going away after just a few months, but it’s not clear why Chiang is departing after such a short stint in the role. At the time of Chiang’s promotion, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma described the new chief operating officer role as a first for Xbox, “with end-to-end P&L responsibility across content, hardware, platform, and services.” The role was created as part of Xbox’s big “reset.” Chiang reported directly to Sharma, and was promoted to “bring our businesses together under one operating model, making sure we make clear investment decisions, learn from our successes and failures, and hold ourselves accountable for results.” Chiang departs amid rumors that Xbox is preparing more layoffs this month, in November, and January. The sudden and short memo from Sharma, coupled with Chiang’s responsibilities being assigned to other Xbox leaders, makes it seem like this wasn’t a resignation. I asked Microsoft to comment on Chiang’s departure, and the company refused to discuss the circumstances of her exit. “We don’t discuss individual personnel matters,” says Kari Perez, Xbox vice president of communications. “We’re grateful for Helen’s years of service and wish her well.”

articles.title: Alien: Covenant Follow-Up Adds Prisoners Writer Aaron Guzikowski
articles.summary: A sequel to Ridley Scott's Alien: Covenant is reportedly in the works with Prisoners writer Aaron Guzikowski.
articles.body:
A follow-up to Ridley Scott's Alien: Covenant is reportedly in the works with Prisoners writer Aaron Guzikowski.

A continuation of the sci-fi horror franchise has started to pick up steam, according to The Hollywood Reporter . Scott is in the mix as a producer, with Guzikowski, who previously worked with Scott on HBO's Raised by Wolves , set to pen its script.

The new Alien film seems to be in its early stages, with much of its plot remaining a secret for now. However, the report did state that it will not be a sequel to 2024's Alien: Romulus and is instead expected to share ties with Scott's Prometheus and Alien: Covenant films. The plan is for its story to include Michael Fassbender's David, though the actor is not attached to return quite yet.

No director has been chosen for now, with Scott only involved as a producer along with Scott Free's Michael Pruss. THR said Scott specifically went to Guzikowski to help get the ball rolling on the project, which he announced in August.

Although there is much work to be done, there is no doubt a large section of Scott fans who will be happy to see more from David the Android. Fassbender first played the character in 2012's Prometheus before returning for its Covenant sequel in 2017. As other Alien projects have come and gone in the years since, how Scott might finish his offshoot trilogy largely remained a mystery.

As for Alien: Romulus, a sequel to the Cailee Spaeny and David Jonsson-starring horror movie was said to still be in limbo. Scott said in August that he thought the first film "was OK" when confirming he intended to return to the franchise because it "needs some help." Although a proper follow-up was said to be in the works as of late 2024, all we've really heard since then is that Fede Alvarez would produce – not direct – whatever came next.

Alien: Romulus - The 10 Biggest Burning Questions

For now, information about the next Alien movie's cast and plot is unclear. While we wait for Scott and Guzikowski to deliver updates, you can read about the long history of Alien and Predator crossovers .

articles.title: Zendaya Sets Best Actress Oscar Campaign for Dune: Part 3
articles.summary: Zendaya will reportedly campaign in the Best Actress category for her role as "Chani" in Dune: Part III in the upcoming Oscars race.
articles.body:
Zendaya will reportedly campaign in the Best Actress category for her role as Chani in Dune: Part III in the upcoming Oscars race.

“The move marks a shift from the first two films, where she was positioned in supporting actress,” said Variety . “The decision reflects Chani’s expanded role in the story.”

This larger, different role for Zendaya’s character in Dune: Part III has not gone unnoticed. IGN’s Jesse Schedeen recently wrote that “everything we’ve seen of Dune: Part Three so far suggests Chani is playing a vastly different role compared to the source material [Frank Herbert’s book Dune Messiah]. Her status quo is completely different. She isn’t Paul’s faithful concubine, pining for the day she can proudly bear his children. She’s rejected Paul and everything he stands for, preferring instead to live as a true Fremen, totally free and a servant to no one.”

It should be noted that none of the actors in either of the past two Dune movies have earned either an Oscar or a Golden Globe nomination for those films. Both Dune movies, however, were nominated in technical categories.

Zendaya has enjoyed a stellar year as an actor , earning praise for The Drama and starring in the two highest-grossing movies of 2026, Spider-Man: Brand New Day and The Odyssey .

The leading entertainment industry awards prognosticators at GoldDerby , however, don’t have Zendaya as a hopeful in either of the Oscars’ actress categories for any of her films. (They currently have her Odyssey co-stars Anne Hathaway and Samantha Morton as the leading contenders to earn a Best Supporting Actress nomination for that film.)

GoldDerby does, however, have Zendaya in the running for a Golden Globe nomination as Best Film Comedy/Musical Actress for The Drama and as TV Drama Actress for the final season of Euphoria . They also have her in the running for a Screen Actors Guild nomination as TV Drama Actress for Euphoria.

The Academy recently altered their rules ahead of next year’s Oscars, including updating their positions on AI and allowing multiple nominations for the same actor in the same category.

The 99th Academy Awards will air live on ABC and Hulu on Sunday, March 14, 2027, at 7 p.m. ET/4 p.m. PT. It will be the third year in a row that Conan O’Brien has hosted the Oscars ceremony.

articles.title: Indie Game Dev Takes Down Vibe-Coded Zombie Shooter After San Francisco Officials Condemn 'Dehumanizing' Game
articles.summary: The developer of a zombie game set in San Francisco has removed the game from online marketplaces and issued a public apology after city officials condemned the title for depicting its homeless people as ‘zombies.’
articles.body:
The developer of a zombie game set in San Francisco has taken down the game and issued a public apology after city officials condemned the title for depicting its citizens as ‘zombies.’

Tenderloin Night Shift was a vibe-coded, first-person shooter created by independent developer Pierre-Louis Biojout over the course of a weekend using OpenAI’s Codex. As you’ve probably inferred by its title, the game takes place in San Francisco’s Tenderloin neighborhood, an area infamous for its high crime rates and unhoused population that’s often compared offhandedly to Los Angeles’s Skid Row.

In the game, players use a gun to rid the Tenderloin of ‘zombies.’ Some of these undead enemies wear construction uniforms or whiz by on motorized scooters, while others wear food delivery backpacks, having clearly been infected while on the job. Still others are depicted doing the ‘fentanyl fold,’ a position where the body is bent forward at the waist, most usually displayed by fentanyl users who seem to have been frozen while standing upright.

“San Francisco couldn’t fix the tenderloin, so I monetized it,” Biojout said on social media. In the game, he sold digital ad space for $100 per week, which accounts for some of the real-world companies seen on billboards within his polygonal recreation of the neighborhood.

It didn’t take long for San Francisco city officials to take notice of the title. Speaking to NCB Bay Area , Mayor Daniel Lurie said, “There’s no accounting for taste or people’s terrible ideas. This is a bad one, and we reject it. It doesn’t speak for San Francisco values.”

In a statement to the San Francisco Chronicle, Supervisor Bilal Mahmood, who represents the Tenderloin, dubbed the game “deeply disturbing and unacceptable.”

“Turning violence against real people, including unhoused people, into entertainment is dehumanizing and should never be normalized,” he said. “I’m encouraged to see that the majority of San Franciscans recognize that this crosses a line and refuse to stand for it.”

While Biojout was previously boasting about the backlash on his social media accounts, he later removed the game from his online platform and issued a public apology over how his project depicted San Francisco’s citizens. He also revealed that he’d been inspired by an Alcatraz-themed Call of Duty map and said he often passes by the Tenderloin on his way to work.

“The game was not intended to provoke or to depict shooting real people. Its characters draw on a broad cross-section of San Francisco, across different backgrounds and walks of life, including people who work in tech. The familiar city details and Easter eggs are part of what makes it fun to play with friends,” he told the Chronicle .

Speaking to NBC Bay Area, Bijout said, “It was not intended to depict shooting real people or to target a particular demographic or group.”

Additionally, Biojout revealed that he refunded advertisers who promoted his game and removed all of his social media posts about it. He also donated the game’s total revenue to the Delancey Street Foundation , a nonprofit organization based in San Francisco that provides rehabilitation services and vocational training to convicted criminals and those suffering from substance abuse.

“I built and posted a zombie game set on San Francisco streets. The setting and the way I promoted it showed poor judgment. Targeting people struggling with addiction or homelessness was never my intention,” he wrote on Twitter/X .

The game was available on Biojout's NanoCorp AI website, a platform that runs online businesses using AI agents. It has since been removed, and the page is no longer available at the time of writing.

articles.title: World Series Game 1 Discussion: Milwaukee Brewers (0-0) vs Tampa Bay Rays (0-0)
articles.summary: Jacob Misiorowski and Nick Martinez are the starters for Game 1 of the World Series
articles.body:
A game 44 years in the making. At long last, Game 1 of the World Series is finally here. The Milwaukee Brewers will face the Tampa Bay Rays to determine who will be the champion in 2026.

Both teams are seeking their first World Series title. The Rays have been here twice before, in 2008 and again in 2020. The Brewers have been just once before, all the way back in 1982.

Both teams were the best in their league this year. The Brewers ran through the National League with a 103-59 record, winning the NL Central by 14 games. The Rays won the AL East by 4.5 games. In the LDS, the Brewers dispatched the San Diego Padres in four games, while the Rays swept the New York Yankees in three. Then in the LCS, the Brewers swept the Dodgers in four games while the Rays fell behind to the Cleveland Guardians 2-1 through three games, but then rattled off three wins in a row to beat Cleveland in six.

The Rays have had three full days off since their last game. The Brewers have had a week off. Finally, after all the anticipation, we are back to baseball.

Also back to baseball is Brewers veteran ace Brandon Woodruff. Woodruff hasn't pitched in a game since the 4th of July, but he has recovered from a shoulder injury and after throwing live BP to the Brewers top hitters during the week, Woodruff was put on the 26 man roster for the World Series.

"I expressed how I felt about things and kind of where I was and I was very truthful and very open. It came down to I want one thing, whether I was on the roster or not, and that's to win. So whatever was decided, I was good with." Woodruff said.

"We feel like there's a window where he can help us. That was the whole decision. This isn't a wow, we love Woody, he's great for the organization, because he already said to us, I don't want to be a sympathy pick. I want to be a pick because I can help the team. Then you go through all the things and say, can he help us? The answer is yes, he can definitely help us." Pat Murphy said.

The Brewers removed Chad Patrick to make room for Woodruff. Patrick had not pitched in either the NLDS or NLCS.

Woodruff will not be starting Game 1, however. That honor, unsurprisingly, belongs to Jacob Misiorowski. Misiorowski has started each Game 1 of the postseason for the Brewers. He hasn't been his usual sharp self that he was during the regular season, which can partially be attributed to fatigue after a long year with more innings than he's ever thrown in his life. Even though he hasn't pitched as deep into games or been as sharp, he's still kept the Brewers in those games and the Brewers have won both of his starts.

On the flip side, the Rays will have Nick Martinez on the mound, allowing an extra day of rest for Tampa's aces Drew Rasmussen and Freddy Peralta. Martinez had a 3.10 ERA in the regular season. In his two starts in the postseason, Martinez went 3.2 IP and allowed two earned runs in his start against the Yankees. Then in the ALCS, Martinez went 5.1 IP, allowing just two hits and one run.

The Brewers are shaking things up a little with their lineup. Jackson Chourio remains in the leadoff spot, that's unchanged. But following him is Jake Bauers batting second and Christian Yelich batting third. Then William Contreras is batting cleanup, followed by Brice Turang and Garrett Mitchell. Cooper Pratt is at shortstop batting seventh while Sal Frelick and David Hamilton round out the bottom of the order. That's three righties in the lineup each with two lefties in between them.

The Rays lineup is also intriguing. Yandy Diaz and Jonathan Aranda are batting 1-2 atop the order. That's not new. But Chandler Simpson, the speedster, with a whopping zero career home runs in his two years in the league, is batting 3rd, a traditional power spot. His role is to get on base for the real power hitter batting cleanup, Junior Caminero. Liam Hicks and Jonny Deluca fill out the rest of the middle of the order. Then Victor Mesa Jr, Ben Williamson, and Taylor Walls round out the bottom of the lineup.

It's the Brewers and the Rays in the 122nd World Series. Here we go.

articles.title: Xbox's First-Ever Chief Operating Officer Leaves Role Just Three Months After It Was Created
articles.summary: Helen Chiang, Xbox’s first-ever chief operating officer, has abdicated the role just three months after it was created, as told by CEO Asha Sharma in an internal memo today.
articles.body:
Helen Chiang, Xbox’s first-ever chief operating officer, has abdicated the role just three months after it was created, as told by CEO Asha Sharma in an internal memo today.

The memo, verified by The Verge , included a brief statement from Sharma regarding Chiang’s exit. “Helen Chiang is leaving Microsoft today. I’m grateful for her years of service and wish her well,” Sharma said. “We’ll share more on COO leadership as plans are finalized.”

Chiang had been with Xbox for an astonishing 21 years. Previously, she was in charge of the Minecraft franchise, and shifted roles to chief operating officer in July 2026.

Xbox and IKEA Furniture Collaboration Photos

The reason for Chiang’s promotion and the job duties of the COO were outlined in a statement by Sharma amid news of Xbox’s massive restructuring this summer. According to Sharma, the role was necessary to “work toward a shared goal, make the right tradeoffs, and get things done” as Xbox’s headcount grew and the company became “more fragmented.”

“For the first time, we are establishing a Chief Operating Officer with end-to-end P&L responsibility across content, hardware, platform, and services. Helen Chiang has been promoted to this role and will report directly to me,” Sharma said at the time.

“Over nearly two decades at Xbox, Helen has helped build some of our most important businesses, from Xbox Live to leading Mojang and the Minecraft franchise. She will bring our businesses together under one operating model, making sure we make clear investment decisions, learn from our successes and failures, and hold ourselves accountable for results.”

As noted by The Verge, the reason for Chiang’s brief tenure in this specific role has not yet been divulged, but it’s certainly a striking move, given her 21 years with the company prior to this.

Xbox is predicted to continue layoffs as part of its ongoing internal restructuring, with 3,200 total employees expected to lose their jobs this year. Several studios have been divested as a result of this rework, though some have managed to find their footing, as is the case with Double Fine .

Others, however, remain in limbo; Arkane Lyon, the studio that’s currently working on Marvel’s Blade , faces closure as soon as mid-November if a buyer isn’t found. The studio was also impacted by the reshuffling at Microsoft, leaving both fans and industry insiders biting their nails in hope that the project finds a new home.

Other companies in the games industry aren’t faring any better. Just this week, EA announced the closure of 30-year-old RPG powerhouse BioWare , known for making games like Dragon Age, Jade Empire, and Mass Effect. The next Mass Effect game was also canceled, prompting worldwide outcry from players and calls for a boycott.

A full-length trailer for the game was also leaked online, rubbing more salt in the wound thanks to just how fantastic it looked. And while fans are crossing their fingers that EA either sells BioWare’s IP or hands them over to another studio, analysts say this isn’t likely. Oh, well — at least the Prime Video series is still alive.

articles.title: Avengers: Doomsday Casts Sandra Hüller in Cameo Role
articles.summary: Marvel has reportedly cast Sandra Hüller in Avengers: Doomsday for a secret cameo role.
articles.body:
Marvel has reportedly cast Sandra Hüller in Avengers: Doomsday for a secret cameo role.

Information about the last-minute addition comes from The Hollywood Reporter , which said the Project Hail Mary star will appear on screens when Earth's Mightiest Heroes take on Robert Downey Jr.'s Doctor Doom this December. Although much of that cast and their parts in the movie have been confirmed, details about Hüller's role were not shared.

Marvel Studios and directors Joe and Anthony Russo almost certainly have plans for plenty of superhero moments and surprises. How Hüller fits into that plan remains to be seen, but considering fans had already speculated about her involvement in recent days, some of the less patient Marvel Cinematic Universe enjoyers are probably already doing their best to piece together Doomsday's mysteries early.

Hüller is a German actor with a decades-long career on movie and TV screens. She was nominated for Actress in a Leading Role at the 2024 Oscars for her part in Anatomy of a Fall, but is also known for her parts in films like Digger, The Zone of Interest, and Fatherland. If you missed her in any of those movies, there's a good chance you caught her playing Eva Stratt, a role that we called one of the best parts of Ryan Gosling's Project Hail Mary .

As for her Marvel introduction, all we know for now is that she'll appear in a cameo part, meaning she probably won't show up for much of its 2-hour-and-45-minute runtime . Like major stars – including Harry Styles and Charlize Theron – before her, it's possible that we could only see Hüller's character during a stinger moment shown during the film's credits sequence. There's at least little reason to suspect that's not on the table, especially considering Marvel will use Doomsday's plot to set up the release of Avengers: Secret Wars in December 2027.

Doomsday is out in just a few short months, but that clearly hasn't stopped Marvel from revealing new information for what's gearing up to be one of the year's biggest releases. Even more about the movie is expected to be revealed at the MLB World Series , which is just a few hours after this piece's publication. THR noted that the Russo brothers are knee-deep in post-production for the film ahead of its December 18, 2026, premiere.

articles.title: Tomb Raider, 30 años de leyenda con tres Lara Croft diferentes: del mito a la humanidad
articles.standfirst: Analizamos a Lara Croft, el personaje que le ha dado vida a una franquicia legendaria durante tres décadas y con tres versiones que diferenciamos claramente.
articles.summary: Analizamos a Lara Croft, el personaje que le ha dado vida a una franquicia legendaria durante tres décadas y con tres versiones que diferenciamos claramente.
articles.body: Tomb Raider cumple 30 años y Lara Croft es un personaje que no necesita casi ni presentación, pero lo que muchos quizá no saben es que en realidad podríamos hablar de tres versiones diferentes de la aventura —posiblemente— más famosa de la industria del videojuego. Es fácil reconocer a Lara. Su rostro es sinónimo de acción, aventuras, disparos y plataformas. Para muchos, es el origen de otras grandes sagas, como Uncharted, así como uno de los personajes que revolucionó el género. Tras el lanzamiento de su primer título, algo cambió en la industria, y muchos descubrieron que había una forma diferente de jugar y entender los videojuegos. Pero aunque todo esto es algo que ligamos muy fácilmente al personaje de Lara, depende de la época en la que lo hagamos. La división de Lara Croft en eras y versiones no depende de la cronología en su sentido más estricto. Sí, se divide en años, pero también en sensaciones. Por un lado tenemos a la primera Lara Croft. La clásica. La de toda la vida. La que muchos de nosotros conocimos cuando apenas éramos unos críos. Su origen se remonta al primer juego, el Tomb Raider de 1996, y la podemos reconocer al instante. Carismática. Fuerte. Independiente. Resolutiva. Autosuficiente. Ingeniosa. Segura de sí misma. Aquella primera Lara era una mujer de armas tomar capaz de resolverlo todo por su propio pie sin ayuda de nadie. Con las tres primeras entregas —las más legendarias de todas para muchos— estableció su figura como una de las grandes del videojuego. Era casi un símbolo cultural. Un fenómeno tal que hasta acabó llegando al cine 5 años después con la mítica versión de Angelina Jolie. Hoy dicen que las cintas han envejecido bastante mal, pero por aquel entonces era un hitazo: que un videojuego tuviese su propia película no era algo que se viese todos los días. La existencia de aquella Lara dio lugar a una leyenda. Una leyenda que se extendió durante seis juegos. Entre 1996 y 2003, conocimos a aquella primera Lara Croft más resolutiva e independiente. No necesitábamos saber casi nada sobre su pasado o sobre su origen porque el presente era espectacular. Aquella mujer con dos pistolas gemelas, coleta y gafas de Sol convirtió su silueta en algo fácilmente reconocible, tanto fuera como dentro de la consola. Por supuesto, todo fue gracias a la aventura, el motor principal de aquellos primeros juegos. El placer de explorar tumbas, resolver puzles, superar plataformas y enfrentarse a toda clase de peligros junto a ella era una sensación indescriptible. Entre el primer y el sexto juego, esto fue evolucionando, ampliando posibilidades y escenarios, pero siempre con cuidado de mantener la fórmula. Por desgracia, su tremendo éxito produjo que la fórmula se quemase. A casi año por juego entre principales y spin-off, Lara se resintió. Siempre era más de lo mismo y aquello empezó a no ser suficiente. Salieron juegos no tan buenos y se notaba que Core Design —desarrolladora principal— estaba acusando el exceso de trabajo continuado: sus juegos ya no se sentían tan refrescantes. Convirtieron a aquella primera Lara Croft en una leyenda que no necesitaba ni que el jugador viese cómo se transformaba en heroína, porque ya lo era, pero mantener vivo a aquel icono exigía encontrar nuevas maneras de presentarlo a la industria... y no siempre se consiguió. Pero, ¿cómo lograrlo? ¿Cómo podías modernizar a un personaje tan mítico como ella sin perder su esencia? No era una tarea sencilla darle un lavado de cara sin dejar a un lado aquello que la hizo especial. La Lara clásica, su carisma, su independencia y el impacto de Tomb Raider en 1996. Cerrar con el desgaste de la fórmula y la crisis de la etapa de Core Design. Tras The Angel of Darkness, Tomb Raider se tomó un descanso y cambió de identidad... en más de un sentido. Aunque Eidos Interactive seguía teniendo el control de la distribución, hubo un cambio de estudio. Core Design se despidió de Lara tras casi una década al timón. Le sustituyó Crystal Dynamics, un prestigioso estudio que había demostrado gran habilidad con los plataformas tras lanzar títulos tan potentes como Gex, Legacy of Kain o Soul Reaver. En 2006, tres años después del último Tomb Raider —tampoco es que dejasen descansar demasiado a la franquicia—, Lara regresó, pero era diferente. El nuevo estudio intentó mantener la esencia de los primeros juegos, pero con cambios inevitables: tenían que recuperar la confianza del público y para ello trajeron a una nueva Lara. Mantuvo su seguridad y su ingenio, así como su condición de aventurera experimentada. No obstante, su versión fue más cercana. Crystal Dynamics empezó a profundizar en sus emociones, sus relaciones y su pasado. La nueva Lara era la misma de siempre, pero inició búsquedas muy personales (como la de su madre) y amplió su biografía con numerosos datos hasta la fecha. Legend recuperó la fórmula, Anniversary reinterpretó el sentido de la aventura original y Underworld amplió la escala de la exploración mientras tejía diversos hilos argumentales. Hasta cierto punto se logró, ya que los juegos no salieron mal en general. No obstante, quedó lejos de esa gran Lara de 1996 que enamoró al mundo. La suya fue, en todo caso, una transición. Esta nueva Croft, la segunda para nosotros, fue el puente entre generaciones, determinando la nueva identidad de la aventurera, pero sin perder su esencia, al darle un mayor trasfondo. Logró sobreponerse a la situación tras el batacazo de The Angel of Darkness, manteniéndose muy ligada a su pasado, pero con más matices e interpretaciones. Y entonces llegó 2013. Más allá del pequeño escarceo de Guardian of Light, Tomb Raider permaneció en las sombras durante 5 años hasta que Square Enix tomó el papel de distribuidor. Crystal Dynamics se mantuvo en su sitio, pero con otro enfoque: se presentó a una nueva Lara Croft, la tercera, muy distinta a lo que conocíamos hasta ahora. Se reinventó la forma en la que entendíamos al personaje. Esta nueva Lara era inexperta y vulnerable. Rompió con sus antecesoras, reconstruyendo la aventura hasta el punto de convertirla casi en una prueba de supervivencia. Se mantuvo ese toque cinematográfico más propio de la segunda Lara, pero la narrativa humanizó al personaje hasta un nivel que no habíamos visto nunca. Generó críticas. Hubo jugadores que apreciaron ese lado desconocido de Lara. Resultó más fácil empatizar con ella, pero también hubo quienes consideraron que se perdía parte de su fortaleza. Ya no se sentía invencible, como la de la leyenda. No obstante, era cuestión de tiempo. Desde el Tomb Raider (a secas) de 2013 hasta Shadow of the Tomb Raider vimos cómo esa Lara Croft se iba pareciendo cada vez más a la primera, pero nunca del todo. Siempre fue más humana. Tenía más matices. Siempre afrontando el peso de sus decisiones, se notaba cada vez más experimentada. Cogió un poco de la primera y un poco de la segunda, siendo cada vez más independiente, pero sin olvidarse de su familia y su pasado. Aprendió a ser sigilosa. Ya no era tan impetuosa, pues el riesgo era mucho más real para ella. Fue consolidando poco a poco una nueva identidad. Una que, con el tiempo, trajo más aplausos que críticas. Con el tiempo, la nueva trilogía logró construir a una Lara completamente nueva, pero que podíamos reconocer también de un solo vistazo. Heredó el espíritu de la primera y la vista atrás de la segunda, pero con un enfoque mucho más humano. Sería, de hecho, la más completa, puesto que en la primera solo conocimos a la aventurera, en la segunda empezamos a ver su pasado y en la tercera se sumó todo eso a su verdadera identidad. Convirtió su evolución personal en el centro de la experiencia incluso por encima de la aventura y, por primera vez, nos preguntamos ¿quién es Lara? Pero, ¿cuál es la verdadera Lara Croft? ¿Existe realmente? Lo cierto es que las tres lo son, pero cada una lo es de una manera diferente. Son tres maneras de entender al mismo personaje. La primera, la clásica, hizo de su nombre y su apellido un icono de la cultura popular que hoy día sigue vivo. No necesitaba que supiésemos quién era para admirarla. Su carisma, su fuerza, su independencia y su capacidad para salir airosa de cualquier peligro eran más que suficientes como para que pasásemos horas pegados a la pantalla. La segunda hizo de puente. Intentó actualizar la imagen de la clásica a los tiempos modernos, otorgándole un mayor peso y trasfondo a su historia personal sin perder su esencia original. Unió a dos generaciones. Por su parte, la tercera demostró que podíamos entender a Lara de otra manera. Nos permitió entender sus miedos y motivaciones. Ganó en humanidad, aunque a cambio perdió parte de ese misterioso encanto del que hacía gala. Al final, cada una ganó algo y perdió otra cosa a cambio. Ninguna fue igual a la anterior, y quizá es por eso que resulta tan difícil quedarse con una sola. Porque, aunque podamos preferir una versión sobre otra, todas han hecho de Lara Croft lo que hoy día es. A fin de cuentas, treinta años después seguimos hablando de ella, y quizá esa sea la mejor prueba de que, por mucho que cambie y por mucho que podamos hablar de tres Laras, ninguna sea la verdadera. Lo que de verdad importa es que siempre ha tenido la capacidad de convertir cada aventura en una nueva oportunidad de descubrirnos quién es.

articles.title: Barnes & Noble Has the First 500-Piece Dungeon Crawler Carl Jigsaw Puzzle for Sale
articles.body:
The Dungeon Crawler Carl series has blown up this year in many ways, but it's the incredibly fast expansion into merchandise has been truly impressive for the franchise. There are T-shirts, graphic novels, action figures, tabletop games, and even a halloween costume available to buy already, but now you can add jigsaw puzzles to that list.

Spotted on Reddit yesterday , there is a new 500-piece DCC puzzle now available at Barnes & Noble Stores. It's called "Meet the Crawlers" and features a full cast of familiar characters from the books, including Carl and Donut.

Surprisingly, this isn't even the first official Dungeon Crawler Carl jigsaw puzzle. There's a 250-piece that was spotted at Barnes & Noble about eight months ago from the same brand, Kingdom of Threads. So if you've been wanting to combine your love of puzzling with your love of Dungeon Crawler Carl, you've apparently got options now.

With the popularity of the upcoming tabletop adaptations from Renegade studios, it's not surprising to see Matt Dinniman's LitRPG story getting the puzzle treatment. Kingdom of Threads may not be one of the most popular puzzle brands out there, but they have already been partnering with other major book fandoms like ACOTAR and Fourth Wing for some time.

As of right now, there are only three Dungeon Crawler Carl puzzles available to buy. The 500-piece puzzle is the highest piece-count available, though, so you'll have to wait for more options if you're looking for a challenge. The "Meet the Crawlers" puzzle features custom art by Levi Cleeman and makes for a great poster once you've pieced the whole thing together.

If you're in the market for something more exciting than a jigsaw puzzle, there are multiple tabletop adaptations you can currently preorder. There's the Dungeon Crawler Carl RPG and the Dungeon Crawler Carl Unstoppable Board Game, both of which are releasing on December 1.
